# Overview of Part 05: Advanced R

To transition from an R data analyst to a senior R software engineer and package author, you need to understand how R works under the hood:

1. **`01_oop_s3_s4_r6.R`** — Object-Oriented Programming across S3 (generic dispatch), S4 (formal typed slots), and R6 (encapsulated mutable reference classes).
2. **`02_functional_programming_and_metaprogramming.R`** — Closures, function factories, higher-order functions (`Reduce`, `purrr`), environments, and Non-Standard Evaluation (NSE / AST manipulation).
3. **`03_error_handling_debugging_performance.R`** — Condition handling (`tryCatch`), memory pre-allocation, hash-environment memoisation, and multi-core `parallel` computing.

---

# Comparing R's Object-Oriented Systems

| Feature | **S3** | **S4** | **R6** |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Paradigm** | Functional OOP (Method belongs to Generic) | Functional OOP (Multiple Dispatch) | Encapsulated OOP (Method belongs to Object) |
| **Semantics** | Copy-on-modify (Immutable value semantics) | Copy-on-modify | Reference semantics (In-place mutation) |
| **Definition** | `structure(list(...), class = "my_class")` | `setClass("MyClass", slots = c(...))` | `R6Class("MyClass", public = list(...))` |
| **Primary Ecosystem** | Base R (`lm`, `data.frame`), `tidyverse`, `tidymodels` | Bioconductor, `Matrix`, `sp` | `shiny`, `mlr3`, stateful clients |

```{r s3-example}
# Clean S3 Class & Generic Method Example
new_model_metric <- function(name, value, higher_is_better = TRUE) {
  structure(
    list(name = name, value = value, higher_is_better = higher_is_better),
    class = "model_metric"
  )
}

print.model_metric <- function(x, ...) {
  direction <- if (x$higher_is_better) "(+)" else "(-)"
  cat(sprintf("[%s %s]: %.4f\n", x$name, direction, x$value))
  invisible(x)
}

rmse_metric <- new_model_metric("RMSE", 2.3415, higher_is_better = FALSE)
auc_metric  <- new_model_metric("ROC-AUC", 0.9482, higher_is_better = TRUE)
print(rmse_metric)
print(auc_metric)
```

# Function Factories, Closures & Hash-Environment Caching

Because every function in R captures a reference to its enclosing environment, we can build fast $O(1)$ hash-table caches using `new.env(hash = TRUE)`:

```{r closure-cache}
make_running_stats <- function() {
  n <- 0L
  mean_val <- 0.0
  m2 <- 0.0
  # Welford's online algorithm for O(1) streaming mean & variance
  list(
    update = function(x) {
      n <<- n + 1L
      delta <- x - mean_val
      mean_val <<- mean_val + delta / n
      delta2 <- x - mean_val
      m2 <<- m2 + delta * delta2
      invisible(NULL)
    },
    summary = function() {
      c(n = n, mean = mean_val, sd = if (n > 1L) sqrt(m2 / (n - 1L)) else NA_real_)
    }
  )
}

tracker <- make_running_stats()
for (v in c(12, 15, 18, 22, 14, 19)) tracker$update(v)
round(tracker$summary(), 3)
```

# Non-Standard Evaluation (NSE) & Code as Data

```{r metaprogramming}
# Building a dynamic SQL/filter expression generator from user symbols
build_summary_expr <- function(metric_col) {
  col_sym <- substitute(metric_col)
  bquote(mean(.(col_sym), na.rm = TRUE))
}

generated_call <- build_summary_expr(mpg)
cat("Generated R Call:", deparse(generated_call), "\n")
cat("Evaluated on `mtcars`:", eval(generated_call, envir = mtcars), "\n")
```
